name: Lifespan
question: Typical (or record) life length, from hours to millennia.

items.name: Adult mayfly
items.fact: Adult mayflies have no working mouths; they live only to mate.

items.name: Fruit fly
items.fact: Fruit flies are one of the most studied animals in genetics.

items.name: Golden hamster
items.fact: Almost all pet hamsters descend from a few hamsters caught in Syria in 1930.

items.name: House mouse (in captivity)
items.fact: Mice can squeeze through gaps about the width of a pencil.

items.name: Dog
items.fact: Small dog breeds tend to live longer than large ones.

items.name: Cat
items.fact: The oldest cat on record lived to 38.

items.name: Horse
items.fact: A horse's age can be estimated from its teeth.

items.name: Brandt's bat (record)
items.fact: This tiny bat weighs about 7 g but can live over 40 years.

items.name: Human (global life expectancy)
items.fact: Global life expectancy has more than doubled since 1900.

items.name: Cookie the cockatoo (record)
items.fact: Cookie lived at a Chicago-area zoo for almost his whole life.

items.name: Galápagos tortoise
items.fact: Galápagos tortoises can survive a year without food or water.

items.name: Bowhead whale
items.fact: Old harpoon tips found in bowheads revealed some were over a century old.

items.name: Rougheye rockfish (record)
items.fact: Rockfish ages are counted from growth rings in their ear bones.

items.name: Hanako the koi (claimed)
items.fact: Hanako's age was estimated by counting rings on her scales.

items.name: Greenland shark (estimate)
items.fact: Greenland sharks grow only about 1 cm a year.

items.name: Ocean quahog clam (record)
items.fact: The record clam, nicknamed Ming, was born in the 1490s.

items.name: Methuselah bristlecone pine
items.fact: Methuselah's exact location is kept secret to protect it.
